title: Trump and Putin meet at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Alaska
body:
On 15 August 2025, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska. Talks ran from about 11:32 a.m. to 2:18 p.m. local time, roughly two hours and 46 minutes. The meeting was announced as three-on-three: Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and envoy Steve Witkoff for the United States, and Putin, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and aide Yuri Ushakov for Russia. A planned working lunch on economic cooperation was cancelled, and neither leader took questions at the joint press briefing.

Putin described the atmosphere as respectful and constructive and agreed with Trump that Ukraine's security must be ensured. Trump's remarks were subdued and did not specifically mention Ukraine or a ceasefire. No agreement or ceasefire was announced.

Before the summit, Trump had threatened sanctions and tariffs if Russia did not agree to a ceasefire. When his deadline passed on 8 August, he announced the Alaska meeting instead. According to the source, Trump proposed lifting sanctions in exchange for a ceasefire, and Putin reportedly offered to end the war if Ukraine ceded all of Donbas, which President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected. Reuters reported a Russian offer that included Ukrainian withdrawal from Donetsk Oblast, barring Ukraine from NATO and recognition of Crimea's annexation.

After the summit Trump moved away from seeking a temporary ceasefire and toward a full peace agreement. On 18 August he met Zelensky at the White House.
